# Let's match the songs in the playlists to the old_songs list by comparing both title and artist(s).
# We'll build a mapping from song_id to whether it should be archived, and also collect the song_ids to archive.

def normalize(s):
    return s.strip().lower()

# Build a set of (title, artist) tuples for old songs for easy matching
old_song_keys = set()
for song in old_songs:
    title = normalize(song["title"])
    # Each artist may be a comma-separated list, so split and normalize each
    artists = [normalize(a) for a in song["artist"].split(",")]
    old_song_keys.add((title, tuple(sorted(artists))))

# Now, for each song in song_details, check if it matches any old song
songs_to_archive = set()
song_id_to_playlist_ids = {}  # For each song_id, which playlists it is in

for playlist_id, song_ids in playlist_map.items():
    for song_id in song_ids:
        song = song_details[str(song_id)]
        title = normalize(song["title"])
        artists = [normalize(a["name"]) for a in song["artists"]]
        key = (title, tuple(sorted(artists)))
        # Try to match by all artists
        if key in old_song_keys:
            songs_to_archive.add(song_id)
            song_id_to_playlist_ids.setdefault(song_id, []).append(playlist_id)

print("Songs to archive:", songs_to_archive)
print("Song to playlist mapping:", song_id_to_playlist_ids)
